newsitem.title: JORDAN: King Hussein urges Arafat, Netanyahu to agree soon.
newsitem.headline: King Hussein urges Arafat, Netanyahu to agree soon.

text.p: Jordan's King Hussein on Sunday urged Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and Palestinian President Yasser Arafat to reach an accord soon to break a logjam in Middle East peace talks, Petra state news agency said.

It said King Hussein in each of two telephone conversations with the two leaders emphasised the necessity of them reaching a decisive agreement over the long delayed re-deployment of Israeli troops from the West Bank town of Hebron.

"This is especially since the differences had narrowed to the degree it makes it imperative to finally resolve the matter in a way that could allow the negotiating parties to move ahead in implementing the rest of the articles of the existing (interim peace) accord," Petra quoted the King as saying.

Israel's former Labour government agreed over a year ago to redeploy troops away from Hebron, home to 100,000 Palestinians and 400 Jewish settlers, but delayed the pullout after suicide bombings by Moslem militants killed 59 people in Israel in February and March.

Israeli and Palestinian negotiators have been trying to clinch a Hebron deal in nearly three weeks of U.S.-brokered talks. Netanyahu said this week an agreement was close but accused Arafat of procrastinating.
